newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs down on upbeat EPA report, cash bond selling.
newsitem.headline: JGBs down on upbeat EPA report, cash bond selling.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was lower by midday on Friday, due to release of the Economic Planning Agency's annual report, which contained the government's strongest official assessment of the economy in the last five years.
Traders said the downside of JGBs is likely to be limited, however, as the EPA's report is unlikely to lead to an immediate rise in interest rates.
Sentiment was also dampened due to selling of cash bonds by investors, who sold after JGBs posted gains early in the morning, a city bank trader said.
"Some investors had been adamant that they wanted to sell cash bonds when the benchmark 182nd JGB yield fell below 2.25 percent," the trader said.
City banks sold the benchmark bond, when the benchmark 182nd JGB yield fell to 2.245 percent early this morning, the trader said. It was the lowest level for the benchmark JGB yield since April 25.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.295 percent as of 0243 GMT, up from Thursday's close of 2.275 percent.
The September ended the morning session bid-only at 124.95, down from the previous day's close of 125.14.
The EPA said in its annual report released on Friday morning that "the present state of the economy is close to one where we can say it is recovering autonomously, led by private-sector demand".

While stressing it did not want to comment on whether or when interest rates should be raised, the EPA said that two years had passed since interest rates had been cut to rock-bottom levels and that firms and individuals should be aware there is a risk that interest rates may rise.
The EPA's report, however, was not enough to alter the market's view that interest rates are likely to be kept unchanged for at least a while longer, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
"The market's scenario on interest rates is that they will remain steady in the July-September period. The EPA's report has not altered that view," he said.
The upside of JGBs is likely to be limited in afternoon trade on position adjustments ahead of a three-day weekend and a 10-year JGB auction expected next Wednesday, traders said.
